gold: Acute myocardial infarction due to critical stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery, presenting with de Winter ECG pattern evolving to Wellens syndrome

selector.rationale: High troponin level and ECG changes with ST-segment elevation and reciprocal depression, along with coronary angiography showing 95% stenosis of the proximal left anterior descending artery, support myocardial infarction as the most specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Coronary Artery Disease
rejected.why: While present, it is less specific than myocardial infarction given the acute presentation and diagnostic findings.

rejected.label: Hypertensive Heart Disease
rejected.why: Hypertension is noted, but the acute chest pain, ECG changes, and elevated troponin level point more directly to an acute coronary event rather than hypertensive heart disease as the primary diagnosis.
